description: S1 - Camellia (Shrub on left boundary, by chest) - Prune to appropriate points by 0.5m for shape.T1 - Black Elder (left boundary) - reduce overall shape to appropriate points by 0.5m for aesthetics.T2 - Willow-Leaved Pear (Dead tree in decking area) -remove to ground level. T3 - Himalayan Birch (rear boundary) - Reduce to appropriate points by 0.5-2m following BS3998 standards to keep the tree maintained and controlled at a reasonable and aesthetically pleasing size without causing large pruning wounds that would hinder the trees longevity. T4 - Goat Willow (rear boundary) - Reduce overall canopy by approximately 2m to appropriate growth points, following BS3998 standards. The aim of the reduction is to allow more light into the garden, give the birch some space and to create a more visually appealing shape.T5 - Cherry (right boundary) - Remove dead and broken branches. Shape tree for aesthetics by 0.5m.S2- Ceanothus & S3 - Camellia (right boundary, rear garden) - Prune to appropriate points by 0.5m for shape and aesthetics. T6 - Willow-leaved pear (front garden) - Shape overall canopy into an aesthetically pleasing shape.T7 - Ornamental Cherry (front garden) - Remove deadwood. Reduce out of shape branches back to natural canopy shape by 0.5m where necessary for aesthetics.H1 - Copper Beech hedge (front garden, Right side of drive when stood at front door) - Reduce overgrown branches on neighbours side back into the line of the hedge by 0.5-1m. Re-trim top and sides of hedge back into boxed hedge shape. Copper Beech (front garden, left side of drive when stood at the front door) - Re-trim sides to appropriate points. Tops to be reduced to match height of Copper Beech hedge on other side of drive, by 0.5m.
